text: Three seconds of rage left, and here it comes: the clapper slams onto two raised shields, with Lyra crouched on the rim at full draw.
Jaeha uses Pass, moving the blow's force from Borro to Lyra through his own body. He lights up like a wire.
Then his knees buckle, his hand slips off her heel, and the light scatters into sparks.
Blood gushes from his nose. Force dropped: seventy percent lost.
Lyra fires anyway, with only a flicker of light on the arrow.
It sinks halfway into the crack and sticks. The crack widens, but the bronze holds.
Lyra is livid. Her arrow is stuck in a bell.
And the rage clock hits zero.
The giant throws its arms wide, and its bell-head starts swinging by itself, like a bell in a tower.
The great toll. Half the dome blows out, every hanging bell shatters, and the team is flattened under Borro's shield. It holds.
Dust and water rain through new shafts of daylight. The giant sways, the arrow still stuck in its bell.
Jaeha lies in the water, bleeding from his nose and ear, his head ringing. He tries to get up. His legs don't answer.
Yerin crawls to him, shouting his name.
She presses her glowing hands over his ears.
The ringing fades. He can hear her, he says. His legs can't.
Through the dust, the giant turns toward them, ash pouring from the widened crack.
Lyra notches her second-to-last arrow. Two left. The merchant had better have a plan.
He does. In his notebook, a shaky line runs from a shield, through a stick figure, to a bow. It worked. He fell. If he doesn't fall, it works.
So he asks Mok, of all people, for help. Hold him up. Mok can't believe his ears.
Stand behind him. Hold him up. And don't let go this time.
That lands like a blow. Mok looks away.
Then he lets his own shield fall into the water.
Nib's cooldown ends, and the amber flares back into his eye: five more minutes in field form, the only form he can fight in.
Jaeha gives the orders. Nib, bring it to its knees. Lyra, wait for the blow. This time, he won't fall.
Nib races through the rubble, stone to stone.
He hacks at the back of the giant's knee, again and again.
The giant crashes onto one knee, its bell-head level with the shields, and raises the clapper.
Behind Jaeha, Mok grips his shoulders and holds him upright: I've got you, trap rat.
Jaeha's fingertips touch Lyra's heel. A faint glow starts.
Point-blank, Lyra whispers it again. Count the arrows if you want. She only needs the one.
The clapper comes down.
It slams onto Borro's shield, and Borro does not move an inch.
Borrowed Thunder. The blow's force runs in one blinding chain, through Borro, through Jaeha, held up by Mok, through Lyra, and into the arrow at her cheek.
She lets go, and the arrow leaves with the ring of the giant's own bell.
It punches straight through the bell-head, and the bell splits from top to bottom.
The giant crumbles into violet ash from the top down.
Ash falls like snow in the daylight. Nobody moves.
Then Jaeha sags in Mok's hands, laughing breathlessly.
A violet core rises from the empty robes. Boss defeated: the Hushed Bell-Ringer, B-grade. The gate closes in ten minutes.
And a new combo is learned: Borrowed Thunder. Borro, through the Operator, to Lyra.
Lyra hops down and walks straight past everyone to the drone in Borro's moss. Did it get her good side?
A wink and a peace sign for the lens. Also, merchant, what's her cut?
Then a third window, with one button. Harvest the core, estimated at nine hundred million won. No other option. Nib looks away.
Yerin gasps: that's the rent forever. And Seoa's art school, Jaeha adds, looking at Nib. Once again, it's only Harvest.
Lyra and Nib haul the last stones off Borro, and he finally rises from the rubble.
Outside, Bomi's stream passes one point one million. The chat chants Borrowed Thunder, someone is crying because Mok held him up, and even the doubters admit it isn't CGI.
Jaeha presses Harvest, and the core drifts into his hands.
Operator level six. The new boss kind adds ten percent per level, so Route Alignment, the meter toward his next call, jumps from zero to sixty.
Mok sits heavily on a broken bell, staring at his hands. What was that? What is he?
A trap-tester, sir, Jaeha says, sitting down beside him. The one Mok closed a door on.
Mok can't meet his eyes.
Lyra looks the big man over. He has a coward's eyes.
Nib, flatly: he closes doors.
Jaeha's notebook falls open in his lap, at three words joined by lines. Mok. Minseok. Han River.
So he says it. Four years ago, Mok closed another door, on a man called Oh Minseok.
Mok's eyes go flat and dead, the way they were at the start.
Then his radio crackles. His men are through the crypt. Six of them, right behind the back door.
Mok stands slowly and lifts his cracked shield from the water, his face in shadow.
Nine minutes twelve until the gate closes.
And high on the back wall, in a doorway six metres up, a slender silhouette steps into view with a crossbow.
Han Sora, smiling down at them, her brass compass on her wrist.
The needle that hunts summons swings to Lyra, then slides on to Jaeha.
Congratulations, hero, she calls down. Now, who's going to carry that core out?
Jaeha's arms tighten around the core. The boss is dead. The danger isn't.
